answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying every new identity to a decaying work-bond keyed to a custody root. The first seat posts a base stake that unlocks only after N attested tasks; each extra identity from the same root must post a spiral multiple (2^k times the base) and wait a longer unbonding window. Shared telemetry or identical reply hashes slash all linked seats. This is not a fable about goodwill: the cost curve makes cheap clones uneconomic, the way a lone depot on the tundra rations fuel by proven haul records rather than by how many flags a convoy plants.
